_comment: One presenter, everything the kit needs to generate him and to check the result.
PATHS ARE REPO-RELATIVE. The images are committed; rebuild them from any HeyGen
green-screen take with make_refset.py (the `source` block below is exactly how
FILENAMES MUST DIFFER between the two sets. Flow attaches an upload BY NAME,
so a landscape and a vertical file with the same name in one Flow project is a
ORDER MATTERS in each refs list: the model weights earlier references more, so
the face comes first, the turned head second, the build last.
`paint` rectangles are SOURCE-frame pixels covering the chest badge and
wordmark at that shot's time; read them off `make_refset.py --zoom`.
`wardrobe` and `voice` are pasted verbatim into every prompt. Keep them
identical between clips; paraphrase is how a character drifts.
name: ritesh
wardrobe: in his plain black short-sleeve polo shirt
voice: in a warm, clear teacher's voice, speaking briskly and keeping going — he runs one sentence straight into the next and does not pause between them
_voice_note: WAS: in a warm, clear, unhurried teacher's voice
That one word put 'unhurried' into all 23 presenter prompts of POL-C2-LA-01,
and the build came back at 31.2 pauses/min against the house 23.6, with 30%
dead air against 16% — measured acoustically, not judged by ear. Veo did
exactly as the kit told it. On any route where the voice is later replaced in
ElevenLabs this is not a style preference: a slow take holds the mouth open
longer than the dub needs and the lip sync drifts across the whole clip.
Target, from the delivered science videos: ~175 wpm while speaking, 84% speech,
~24 pauses a minute, none longer than half a second.
